title: The OI class
summary: static methods on an abstract class that owns the controller.

say.never: `OI` stands for **Operator Interface**, which is just a fancy name for "the controls". This class is the only place that knows about the gamepad. The rest of the robot asks it questions like "how far forward is the driver pushing?" and never cares which stick that comes from. Nobody ever makes a new OI, and its methods are `static`, so you call them on the class itself.
say.bit: OI (Operator Interface) is the one class that knows about the gamepad. The rest of the robot asks it questions through static methods.

board.code:
robot code  ->  "how hard is the driver pushing forward?"  ->  OI  ->  reads the gamepad

Only OI knows which stick that is.
